title: Data Structures & Algorithms in C++ (Interview-Grade)
tagline: Turn your C++ fluency into problem-solving power.
summary: Turn your C++ fluency into problem-solving power. You implement every core data structure and algorithm from scratch in modern C++ — dynamic arrays, linked lists, stacks/queues, trees, heaps, tries, hash tables, and graphs — then master the algorithmic techniques that dominate technical interviews: two pointers, sliding window, recursion, binary search, sorting, BFS/DFS, shortest paths, greedy, divide-and-conquer, backtracking, and dynamic programming. Every project pairs a working implementation with complexity analysis and the interview patterns it unlocks. Note the division of labour with the c-systems track: c-systems hand-rolls a vector, linked list, hash table and ring buffer in C as exercises in memory ownership and API design, because C ships no containers at all. This track is the algorithms course - complexity analysis, balanced trees, graph algorithms and the design paradigms - and it is where the structures c-systems deliberately defers are taught. This is the shared problem-solving core of the Zero-to-Low-Level-Systems-Elite program: it takes the language from cpp-from-zero and builds the timed, whiteboard-ready algorithmic skill that HFT, AI-chip, and big-tech screens all test.

capstone.title: Autocomplete & Route-Planning Engine (Tested & Benchmarked)
capstone.project: Build a real, CMake-packaged C++ application that combines the data structures you implemented across the track: a trie-backed autocomplete with ranked suggestions (trie + heap), and a route planner over a weighted graph using Dijkstra's algorithm. Unit-test it with GoogleTest, benchmark the hot paths, and document the structures chosen and why.

phases.title: Complexity & Array Foundations
phases.goal: Reason about running time with Big-O and master array techniques: dynamic arrays, two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums, and matrices.

projects.title: Big-O Notation & Measuring Growth
projects.description: Build intuition for asymptotic complexity by implementing the five common complexity classes, deriving Big-O from code, and empirically timing algorithms with std::chrono to watch growth curves diverge.

projects.title: Arrays & Traversal Patterns
projects.description: Master the fundamental array traversal patterns — find max/min, count, accumulate, and in-place modify — using std::vector, and observe why contiguous memory and cache-friendliness make arrays fast in practice.

projects.title: Dynamic Arrays & Amortized Analysis
projects.description: Build a minimal MyVector<T> from scratch with new[]/delete[] and capacity doubling, then prove that push_back is amortized O(1) using the aggregate counting method.

projects.title: The Two-Pointer Technique
projects.description: Implement four classic two-pointer problems — reverse in place, pair-sum on sorted array, remove duplicates, and palindrome check — and prove each is O(n) vs the O(n²) naive approach.

projects.title: The Sliding Window Technique
projects.description: Solve fixed-window and variable-window subarray problems — max-sum of size-k subarray, longest unique substring, minimum-length sum window — in O(n) using a sliding window, and contrast with O(n²) naive solutions.

projects.title: Prefix Sums & Range Queries
projects.description: Build 1D and 2D prefix-sum arrays to answer arbitrary range-sum queries in O(1), implement a difference array for O(1) range updates, and understand the preprocessing vs query time tradeoff.

projects.title: 2D Arrays & Matrix Traversal
projects.description: Implement row-major traversal, spiral and diagonal iteration, and in-place transpose and 90° rotation of a square matrix, expressing all complexity in terms of both m and n.

projects.title: Array Algorithms Toolkit (Finale)
projects.description: Synthesise all Phase 1 techniques — two-pointer, sliding window, prefix sums, and matrix operations — into a single CLI toolkit with a complexity reference table, a benchmark, and a problem-triage decision guide.

phases.title: Linear Structures: Lists, Stacks & Queues
phases.goal: Build the pointer-based linear structures from scratch: singly/doubly linked lists, stacks, queues, deques, and their classic applications.

projects.title: Singly Linked List
projects.description: Build a templated SinglyLinkedList<T> from scratch using raw node pointers, implementing push_front (O(1)), push_back (O(n)), remove, search, traversal, and a correct RAII destructor with full Rule of Five compliance.

projects.title: Doubly Linked List
projects.description: Build a templated DoublyLinkedList<T> with prev/next pointers and head/tail anchors, enabling O(1) insert and delete at both ends and O(1) node removal given a pointer handle.

projects.title: Linked List Algorithms
projects.description: Implement the four classic interview linked-list algorithms — in-place reversal (iterative and recursive), Floyd's cycle detection, slow/fast middle-finding, and sorted list merge — each as a stand-alone O(1)-space program.

projects.title: Stack (LIFO)
projects.description: Implement the Stack ADT two ways — a fixed-capacity array-backed ArrayStack<T,N> with zero runtime allocation and a dynamically growing LinkedStack<T> backed by linked nodes — then compare their complexity and allocation trade-offs.

projects.title: Queue & Circular Buffer
projects.description: Implement the Queue ADT as a linked-node queue with O(1) enqueue/dequeue and then as a fixed-size circular ring buffer with modulo wrap-around, zero runtime allocation, and a count-based full/empty disambiguation.

projects.title: Deque (Double-Ended Queue)
projects.description: Build a Deque<T> backed by a doubly linked list with O(1) push/pop at both ends, then implement the sliding-window maximum using a monotonic deque to show the structure's canonical O(n) application.

projects.title: Applications of Stacks & Queues
projects.description: Implement four canonical algorithms that demonstrate the power of LIFO and FIFO disciplines: balanced bracket checking, Shunting-Yard infix-to-postfix conversion with postfix evaluation, next-greater-element via a monotonic stack, and a BFS level-order traversal preview.

projects.title: LRU Cache
projects.description: Build an O(1) Least-Recently-Used cache by composing std::unordered_map with a hand-written doubly linked list (with sentinel nodes), implementing get and put in strictly O(1) time with correct LRU eviction and move-to-front on access.

phases.title: Recursion, Searching & Sorting
phases.goal: Master recursion and the canonical algorithms: binary search, merge/quick/heap sort, and the analysis that explains why each performs as it does.

projects.title: Recursion & the Call Stack
projects.description: Build factorial, Fibonacci, and exponentiation recursively, trace the call stack frame-by-frame, observe exponential blow-up, fix it with memoisation, and understand tail recursion — tying hardware stack mechanics to algorithmic reasoning.

projects.title: Binary Search & Its Variants
projects.description: Implement classic binary search with overflow-safe mid, then build lower_bound and upper_bound from scratch, search a rotated sorted array, and apply binary search on the answer to an optimisation problem — understanding the loop invariant that makes each variant correct.

projects.title: Elementary Sorts
projects.description: Implement bubble, selection, and insertion sort from scratch with comparison/swap counters, compare their behaviour on sorted, random, and reverse inputs, and understand stability, in-place sorting, and why insertion sort remains relevant inside every production sort library.

projects.title: Merge Sort (Divide & Conquer)
projects.description: Implement merge sort from scratch — the merge step, recursive split, and bottom-up iterative variant — derive T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) via the recursion tree, verify O(n log n) time and O(n) space, and confirm stability with a keyed-record test.

projects.title: Quick Sort & Partitioning
projects.description: Implement Lomuto and Hoare partition schemes, observe the O(n^2) worst case with fixed pivot on sorted input, eliminate it with randomised pivot selection, and handle duplicates efficiently with three-way Dutch National Flag partitioning.

projects.title: Heap Sort & the Binary Heap
projects.description: Build an array-based binary max-heap from scratch with sift_up, sift_down, and O(n) heapify, then implement heap sort (in-place, O(n log n), not stable) and a full priority queue interface — the same heap that powers Dijkstra and std::priority_queue.

projects.title: Choosing a Sort: Analysis, Stability & std::sort
projects.description: Consolidate all six sorting algorithms into a comparison table, prove the Omega(n log n) comparison lower bound with a decision-tree argument, implement counting sort and radix sort from scratch, and learn what std::sort (introsort) and std::stable_sort actually do.

projects.title: Searching & Sorting Toolkit
projects.description: Build a header-only toolkit.hpp exposing binary_search, lower_bound, merge_sort, quick_sort, and heap_sort, then benchmark all five against std::sort and std::stable_sort on random, sorted, and reversed inputs using <chrono>, and write a structured empirical analysis tying the numbers back to algorithmic theory.

phases.title: Trees, Heaps & Tries
phases.goal: Implement hierarchical structures: binary trees and BSTs, balancing, binary heaps/priority queues, tries, and range-query trees.

projects.title: Binary Trees & Traversals
projects.description: Build a binary tree from scratch with RAII cleanup and implement all four traversals — preorder, inorder, postorder (recursive and iterative with an explicit stack), and level-order BFS — to understand how the call stack and data-structure traversal relate.

projects.title: Binary Search Tree
projects.description: Build a full BST with insert, search, and delete (all three cases including two-children/inorder-successor) from scratch, and confirm that inorder traversal always yields sorted output.

projects.title: Tree Algorithms
projects.description: Implement the eight classic interview tree algorithms — height, balanced-check, diameter, LCA, validate-BST, invert, and path-sum — each demonstrating a distinct recursive postorder-reduction pattern.

projects.title: Balanced Trees & Rotations
projects.description: Implement an AVL self-balancing BST from scratch — height-tracked nodes, left/right rotations, all four imbalance cases (LL/RR/LR/RL), and insert with automatic rebalancing — proving that O(log n) height is maintained regardless of input order.

projects.title: Binary Heap & Priority Queue
projects.description: Implement an array-backed max-heap with sift-up push, sift-down pop, and O(n) build_heap, then generalize it as a PriorityQueue<T,Comp> class template that works as min- or max-heap, and apply it to the top-K streaming problem.

projects.title: Trie (Prefix Tree)
projects.description: Build a trie from scratch with 26-slot array children and an end-of-word flag, implementing insert, search, startsWith, and an autocomplete function via DFS-with-backtracking.

projects.title: Range-Query Trees: Fenwick & Segment Tree
projects.description: Build a Fenwick tree (BIT) for O(log n) prefix-sum update and query using the lowbit trick, then build a segment tree supporting both range-sum and range-min queries with point updates, and compare when each structure is appropriate.

projects.title: Tree Toolkit: Huffman Coding
projects.description: Synthesize Phase 4 by building a complete Huffman coding pipeline: frequency table, greedy tree construction with a min-heap, prefix-free codebook generation by tree traversal, encode a string to bits, and decode using the tree as a trie.

phases.title: Hashing & Graphs
phases.goal: Build hash tables and graph algorithms: collision handling, hashing patterns, BFS/DFS, shortest paths, and topological sort.

projects.title: Hash Tables from Scratch
projects.description: Build a HashMap<K,V> with separate chaining, load-factor-triggered resize, and average O(1) insert/find/erase, then compare against std::unordered_map.

projects.title: Open Addressing & Hashing Internals
projects.description: Build a FlatMap<K,V> with linear probing and tombstone deletion, implement double hashing to eliminate clustering, and compare cache behavior against separate chaining.

projects.title: Hashing Interview Patterns
projects.description: Implement five canonical hashing patterns — frequency counting, deduplication, two-sum, group anagrams, and subarray-sum-equals-k — each turning an O(n²) brute force into an O(n) solution.

projects.title: Graph Representations
projects.description: Build a reusable Graph class with adjacency-list and adjacency-matrix representations for directed/undirected weighted graphs, analyze space and time tradeoffs, and load graphs from edge lists.

projects.title: Breadth-First Search
projects.description: Implement BFS with a queue on the Project 4 Graph class to compute shortest unweighted paths, find connected components, and solve a grid maze with an implicit graph.

projects.title: Depth-First Search
projects.description: Implement recursive and iterative DFS on the Project 4 Graph class, detect directed cycles with three-color marking, detect undirected cycles with parent tracking, and enumerate all paths with backtracking.

projects.title: Weighted Shortest Paths & Topological Sort
projects.description: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap priority queue for non-negative weighted shortest paths, and topological sort via both DFS post-order and Kahn's BFS algorithm with cycle detection.

projects.title: Graph Toolkit
projects.description: Synthesise the phase: build a GridPathfinder running BFS and Dijkstra on weighted terrain, implement Union-Find with path compression and union by rank, and apply it to Kruskal-style connectivity.

phases.title: Algorithm Design & Interview Mastery
phases.goal: Wield the big algorithmic paradigms — greedy, divide-and-conquer, backtracking, and dynamic programming — and assemble a tested capstone.

projects.title: Greedy Algorithms
projects.description: Build four greedy classics from scratch — interval scheduling, coin change (with DP counterexample), fractional knapsack, and Huffman coding — proving each correct or wrong via the exchange argument.

projects.title: Divide & Conquer
projects.description: Implement maximum subarray (D&C vs Kadane), inversion counting via merge sort, and fast exponentiation, then apply the Master Theorem to analyze the recurrence of each.

projects.title: Backtracking
projects.description: Implement permutations, subsets, combinations, N-Queens, and a Sudoku solver using the choose/explore/un-choose template, then quantify how pruning reduces nodes visited exponentially.

projects.title: Dynamic Programming I (1D)
projects.description: Implement Fibonacci, climbing stairs, house robber, coin change (minimum coins), and LIS from scratch using both memoization and tabulation, deriving each recurrence from first principles.

projects.title: Dynamic Programming II (2D & Sequences)
projects.description: Implement grid unique-paths, min-path-sum, 0/1 knapsack, LCS, and edit distance with full 2D tables and space-compressed variants, including solution reconstruction for LCS.

projects.title: Bit Manipulation
projects.description: Implement ten canonical bit tricks (check/set/clear/toggle, LSB, popcount, power-of-2, XOR swap, single number, bitmask subsets), explain their two's complement mechanics, and apply them to HFT-style flag operations.

projects.title: Interview Patterns & Problem-Solving Framework
projects.description: Build a systematic problem-solving framework mapping 8 signal patterns to algorithms, implement the same problem two ways with explicit tradeoff analysis, and study the complexity targets and LeetCode strategy that make pattern mastery stick.

projects.title: Autocomplete & Route-Planning Engine (Track Capstone)
projects.description: Build a CMake-packaged, GoogleTest-tested C++ application combining a Trie-backed autocomplete (top-k via heap) and a weighted-graph route planner (Dijkstra), structured as a library + thin CLI with 10 tests covering happy paths and edge cases.
